recipes.name: Pineapple Upside Down Cupcakes
ingredients_raw: 1 (18.25 ounce) package pineapple cake mix (such as Duncan Hines® Pineapple Supreme)
1 tablespoon confectioners' sugar for dusting, or as needed

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Move an oven rack to the middle of the oven. Spray 24 muffin cups with cooking spray.
Spoon 1 teaspoon melted butter into the bottom of each sprayed muffin cup.
Spoon 1 tablespoon brown sugar into each muffin cup. Press a maraschino cherry into the center of the brown sugar in each muffin cup.
Spoon a heaping tablespoon of crushed pineapple on top and compact it with the back of a spoon into an even layer.
Mix pineapple cake mix, pineapple juice, vegetable oil, and eggs in a large bowl with an electric mixer on low speed until moistened, about 30 seconds. Increase speed to medium; mix for 2 minutes.
Pour batter into the muffin cups, filling them to the top; do not overfill.

Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of a cupcake comes out clean, about 20 minutes. Line a work surface with waxed paper. Allow cupcakes to cool at least 5 minutes before inverting muffin cups onto the waxed paper; serve with pineapple and cherry sides up.
Sprinkle cupcakes lightly with confectioners' sugar before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Pineapple Upside Down Cupcakes
raw_recipe.description: These pineapple upside down cupcakes are made with pineapple cake mix, crushed pineapple, and brown sugar, topped with sweet pineapple and red cherry.

video.description: Turn the classic upside down cake into simple mini cakes perfect for gatherings or as quick treats for enjoying one after the other! Prepare a muffin tin by filling each cup with melted butter, brown sugar, maraschino cherry and crushed pineapple. Then make a batter with pineapple cake mix, eggs, pineapple juice and vegetable oil and fill each cup. Bake, cool and serve upside down, sprinkled with a dusting of confectioners’ sugar and just try to eat only one.

review.reviewBody: I've been making this basic recipe for years with a couple differences: I used a yellow cake mix with the juice from the pineapple in place of the water (add water to the juice if necessary). I've used pineapple tidbits and rings cut up to fit instead of the crushed pineapple. Crushed pineapple can sometimes make the cake under it too mushy sometimes. Instead of putting the batter directly into the muffin pan, I used paper liners which is so much easier for lunches and serving at picnics. It's a surprise when they take the paper off to eat it! It's basically sweet enough for me to eat like this but occasionaly I've dusted powdered sugar on top of the cupcakes after slightly cooled. Oh, and if you're a coconut lover, add a little to the brown sugar before laying in the pineapple and cherries. This is a great recipe anyway you make it!

These were moist and very delicious! A big hit. I couldn't find pineapple cake mix and used French vanilla. I took other reviewers suggestions and melted tge butter and mixed it with the brown sugar before spooning into the cupcakes pans. Many reviews said they had difficulty with the cupcakes releasing from the pans so I greased them liberally with butter and then sprayed them with Baker's Joy. I used pineapple tidbits, which I felt made them look more like traditional pineapple upside down cake. I put the tidbits on top of the butter and brown sugar and then pushed the cherry through. I followed the ingredient proportions on the cake mix box because they no longer make 18 oz cake mixes; 1 cup pineapple juice, 1/2 cup oil and 3 eggs. I baked them 24 minutes, rotating them halfway through. I cooled them 10 min. I laid out parchment paper, loosened the cupcakes where there was a slight overrun and inverted them onto the parchment. They released without a hitch and everyone loved them. This one is a keeper!

As suggested by some other readers, I used a yellow cake mix and used pineapple tidbits. The juice from the can was less than a cup. I supplemented with some cherry juice. I used 8 small ramekins and was also able to get 7 cupcakes. Only 1/2 tsp butter is needed on the cupcakes. These cakes are delicious!

These are delicious! I really liked that the ratio of fruit/brown sugar to cake is greater than with a standard cake. I used a classic yellow cake mix with 1 cup pineapple drained from a 20 oz can of pineapple chunks. As another reviewer mentioned, the cake mix was a bit smaller than called for in the recipe (15 oz vs 18 oz), so 1 cup liquid was just right. I cut the pineapple chunks in half and placed 3-4 in each muffin cup with 1/2 maraschino cherry in the center as shown in the photo. Important: when adding the cake batter, fill no more than half full. I made 12 cupcakes directly in the pan (well greased) and 12 in paper muffin cups. There was enough batter remaining to make an additional small (5" cake). The only problem I had was that some of the butter/brown sugar remained stuck in both the pan and the paper cups (hence 4 starts instead of 5), so I probably won't make this for any more than a very casual occasion.

As a child my son would say, "Pineapple Upside Down" and his father and I would say "Cake"! For his 36th birthday I made these using ramekins including a large one, just for him. We don't really like maraschino cherries, so I got some dried Montmorency ones and rehydrated them first and used them instead. I also added the water from the cherries to the pineapple juice to make enough liquid. They were a huge hit with everyone! I will be making this family favorite this way again!!

Delicious and easy. I did use pineapple juice in place of water in the mix and used tidbits instead of crushed pineapple. Tidbits take more time for placement but much prettier outcome I think. The crowd at my Luau LOVED them. They don’t need to know it was a box cake!

This was really easy and delicious! I made it with a regular sized cake yellow mix and made two 8” cakes. I swapped the oil for applesauce and used the pineapple juice in place of water. It was sooooooooo good! Thank you for the recipe!

I think I will use less brown sugar next time and as mentioned by others will mix it with the butter, and maybe even the pineapple before putting it in the cups. I used only cherry 1/2s. I drained the can of crushed pineapple and took the excess moisture out of it so I had less pineapple topping. I used the juice in the cake mix. I made 6 giant and 12 regular cupcakes.

I made these today to take to work potluck. I didn't notice until after first batch that the Duncan Hines pineapple cake mix is no longer 18.25 ounces but it is 15.25. That explains why my batter was so thin. For my next batch I will only add 1 cup of pineapple juice instead of 1 1/3 as the box calls for 1 cup of water. I made them in mini muffin pans and had to be extra careful not to put too much of the topping in. Since it was already thin batter they got very wet with the toppings. I couldn't get them out of the pan.

I think the brown sugar amount could be lessened to 2 teaspoons instead of 1 tablespoon since quite a bit was left in the cups after taking them out. I used cut pineapple pieces instead to make it prettier. Also the amount of batter didn’t fully fill each cup of my 24 cup pan. 2 cakes are actually shorter since I had to split the little bit of batter that was left. They have great taste and are also fluffy. Would make again with my tweaks!

I made it with crushed pineapple (let drain for ten minutes any extra pineaplle left from putting in first add to mix) don't over fill leave an 1/8 space from top... This is my family's new favorite..

I changed to tidbits, 8 in each of the 24 muffin spots. A 20oz of dole tidbits covers it all with about 30 tidbits left over as well as the 1.33C of the juice (although it's not quite as good as it is out of a pineapple juice can). Allow the cupcakes to cool more than 5 minutes before putting them under the wax paper, but not too long to the point where the brown sugar that's reached the top edge hardens and holds them in place. Cover them in more wax paper after they have fully cooled down and then foil on top of that to hide the surprise for transport. Easily in my top 10 desserts of all time, any picnic I go to I end up with an empty tray
The same taste my mom made back in the 1960's when I was at home....

They taste great, but the recipe isn't quite right. It doesn't say whether to drain the pineapple or not. I did because it seemed like it would be way too juicy otherwise. If you use the heaping tablespoon of pineapple, you're going to need at least 2 cans, but 3 would be better. They also stick like crazy. Mine look awful! I spooned the stuck topping onto them and am hoping it'll stick as it cools.

I pretty much used the exact recipe with a few minor adjustments. I emptied the juice from one can of Pineapple tidbits to use in the batter and dehydrated the fruit for 4 hours. I drowned the cups in cooking spray and only sprinkled a few tidbits in each cup to ensure each got at least a few around the cherry. I added 1/3 cup water to make up the difference in the juice. I also cooked them about 25min. I had to scrape them loose with a spatula after resting for 10min. A few didn't make it, but the rest turned out "Blessed from Above".
Perfect size! Great tasting and beautiful to serve.
Easy and yummy and pretty! Used a vanilla cake mix. Ran out of pineapple after 12 muffins. Next time I’ll get 2 cans.

Made as described except no cherries and was using up fresh pineapple. Delicious but very sticky--need a fork to eat. very easy to make. used silicone pans so it came out very easily. Oh I had to use vanilla cake mix because store didn't have pineapple and whenever I use a cake mix I replace the oil with melted butter.
